jobs.title: Senior Talent Acquisition Partner
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About The Role

As our Senior Technical Talent Partner, you’ll lead end-to-end hiring for high-impact tech and non-tech roles, from software engineers to data scientists, ensuring we attract, engage, and hire the best talent in the market. Working closely with engineering leaders, product managers, and senior stakeholders, you’ll design hiring strategies that meet immediate needs while building a sustainable pipeline for the future. If you thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments and love solving complex hiring challenges, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

  • Lead the full-cycle recruitment process for different roles, from sourcing and assessment to offer and onboarding.

  • Partner with tech leaders to understand team roadmaps, define role requirements, and set clear hiring priorities.

  • Build and execute advanced sourcing strategies to engage passive technical talent through LinkedIn, GitHub, Stack Overflow, events, and niche communities.

  • Maintain and grow a strong pipeline of engineers, engineering managers, and product managers for current and future needs.

  • Oversee and optimize our ATS and recruitment processes for speed, accuracy, and candidate experience.

  • Conduct technical and cultural fit assessments in collaboration with engineering teams.

  • Champion our employer brand within the tech community by crafting engaging job descriptions, showcasing projects, and representing the company at events and meetups.

  • Leverage recruitment analytics to track pipeline health and conversion rates—using insights to continuously improve strategies.

What You'll Need

  • Proven experience in tech talent acquisition, ideally in a startup or high-growth tech company.

  • Deep understanding of technical hiring (software engineering, product management, data, DevOps, etc.) and the ability to speak credibly with candidates about their work.

  • Track record of building high quality pipelines and closing hard-to-fill technical roles.

  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with experience influencing senior tech leaders and executives.

  • Data-driven approach to recruitment, using metrics to guide decisions and improvements.

  • Skilled in advanced sourcing methods across multiple platforms and communities.

  • Familiarity with ATS tools (e.g., Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever, or similar).

  • A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset with the ability to balance speed and quality in hiring.

Who Are We?

Thndr was founded on a bold dream to democratize access to investing through smart tech and human-centric design. This is simply our way of saying we give anyone with a smartphone the simple and easy access they need to preserve and grow their wealth. At the same time, we’re shaping the future of investing while actively driving the economies we serve by promoting local investment products.

History has shown that investing is the single greatest way to build long-term wealth, but before Thndr, only a very small percentage of people had access to it due to:

  • High barriers to entry — In the form of excessive minimum account balances, complex, outdated onboarding, and low financial literacy.

  • Irrelevant experience — Catered toward expert traders and financial specialists, therefore alienating the majority of the population.

  • Fragmented offering — Investment products were not gathered in a single, intuitive outlet.

We don't just talk about change, we deliver it. Here's a glimpse into our impact so far:

  • 3 million app downloads

  • $8.8bn in annualized traded value

  • #1 platform in terms of traded value

  • 84% of our users are investing for the first time

  • 65% of our users come from outside of capital cities and have previously had limited access to financial institutions

Building on the success of our core platform, we are continuing to change culture and break down barriers by launching Rumble, the subscription-based investment recommendations platform.

Rumble was born with the vision to empower everyday individuals to build wealth confidently and intelligently through access to timely and in-depth advice from the industry’s top experts.

Going beyond traditional investment advice, it offers long and short-term investment recommendations and financial content through engaging articles and videos that guide users on their financial journey and maximize their returns.

At Thndr, we're looking for people driven by our mission to help us democratize investing across the MENA region.

• Define, implement, and monitor infrastructure security measures.

• Contribute to the security roadmap & backlog.

• Assess security tools and integrate tools as needed.

• Actively mentor members of the security team.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Thndr

Thndr is on a mission to make investing simple and accessible for everyone across the Middle East and North Africa. Since launching in 2019 and going through Y Combinator shortly after, we have grown into Egypt's number one investing app, with millions of people putting their money to work in stocks, gold, mutual funds, and more, many of them investing for the very first time.

We are licensed by Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority and are a member of the Egyptian Exchange. In 2024 we expanded into the UAE under an ADGM license, and in 2025 we became the first remote retail trading member of the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange. That same year, the World Economic Forum named us a Technology Pioneer, the only Egyptian company alongside Apple, Google, Dropbox, and others. In 2026, The Financial Times named us the fastest growing company in Africa. We are backed by investors including Tiger Global, Prosus Ventures, BECO Capital, and Y Combinator, and we are only getting started.

The Team You Would Join

Today, roughly 40% of all transactions on the Egyptian Exchange flow through Thndr. Behind almost everything a user sees or relies on is market data, and the Feed team owns it. Live and delayed prices, statistics, charts, and asset data across every market we operate in all flow through systems we build and run.

We ingest data from different providers, sometimes multiple per market, and expose it to the rest of Thndr through a single, unified feed. Nearly everything downstream depends on it: the live prices users watch, the alerts we fire when something moves, and the limit orders that execute off the numbers we serve. Our users range from first-time investors making a decision about where to put their money, to technical traders who need immediate, actionable insights. Every millisecond matters. When a price arrives late or wrong, it is not a cosmetic bug, it is real money for real people acting on information that has to arrive on time, every time.

On top of that, we are building for scale, and one that is genuinely hard: a feed engineered to handle 100,000+ assets and hundreds of thousands of price updates a second, without dropping a beat.

This is a sensitive system, and a foundational one. Providers fail, connections drop, and infrastructure gives out mid-session, and none of that is an excuse to stop serving users. Much of the hard part is staying correct and available when something upstream breaks: failing over in the middle of an open market, absorbing a provider outage, and keeping the feed flowing when the pieces underneath it do not. You would be working alongside some of our strongest engineers on problems that are unusually hard and unusually consequential, owning systems the rest of the platform quietly depends on.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and operate the feed services that serve market data across Egypt, UAE, US, and soon KSA, processing large volumes of data and events with very low latency and high reliability.

  • Keep the feed available and correct when things break, owning the SLOs and overall health of your services, with strong observability, sensible on-call, and graceful failover when a provider drops or infrastructure gives out mid-market.

  • Understand the different databases and data models we use, Redis, ClickHouse, and Postgres, how each behaves, and when to reach for which.

  • Own the infrastructure the feed runs on. Understand how data reaches us from each provider, and build in redundancy where it matters so a single upstream failure never takes us down.

  • Identify technical debt and reliability risks in your area and steadily improve the systems you own.

  • Raise the bar on quality and operational discipline, and support the engineers around you through code and design reviews and pairing.

What You'll Need

  • A strong track record of designing, shipping, and operating reliable backend systems in production, used by large numbers of people.

  • Real depth in distributed systems, and a clear understanding of what it takes to keep them fast and correct under load and under failure.

  • Comfort owning systems end to end, from design through production and on-call. You care not just about writing the code, but about how it behaves when a provider drops or a node fails.

  • A feel for performance, and the instinct to treat latency and throughput as first-class concerns rather than afterthoughts.

  • Familiarity with our stack, or the confidence to get there quickly: Python, C#, .NET Core, Golang, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Redis, and ClickHouse.

  • A high bar for correctness and operational discipline. You understand what it means to run a system where a mistake has real consequences for real people.

  • A clear, candid communicator who can hold their own with other engineers and work closely with the teams that build on what you provide.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building systems optimized for real-time performance, where latency and throughput are on the line.

  • Experience with ClickHouse or similar OLAP databases, and the query and schema patterns that get the most out of them.

  • Experience in fintech, brokerage, trading, or another regulated, high-stakes domain where correctness and timing matter.

Why this Role

The feed sits underneath almost everything Thndr does. Every price a user watches, every alert we send, and every order that fires does so because the feed delivered the right number at the right moment. It is some of the most performance-critical engineering in the company, the kind of work where being fast and being correct are the same problem, and it matters to millions of people.

If building systems that have to be fast, correct, and trusted without exception sounds like your kind of challenge, and if doing it at real scale across multiple markets excites you, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Role:

Thndr is a fast-moving, highly regulated fintech. You’ll join the Information Security team as a senior information security specialist and work closely with the Information Security Manager. We’re looking for someone who has done this before, works independently and isn’t shy about suggesting a better way.

What You'll Do:

• Turn raw evidence into audit-ready documents and file it requirement by requirement, with the ability to tie down different regulations into one fabric of compliant controls.

• Ability to do gap assessment for different compliance frameworks to identify gaps early and work on introducing and adjusting controls to mitigate gaps.

• Keep policies current: update them to close gaps, manage versions, and make sure policies are aligned with the targeted compliance framework and the regulatory fabric.

• Maintain the scope picture (system description, data flow and network diagrams, asset inventory) and keep it in line with what is actually deployed.

• Pull technical evidence from live systems with engineering, such as access reviews, backups, patching, scans and change records, without disrupting production.

• Run third-party risk: vendor attestations, shared responsibilities and the service provider inventory.

• Run the people side of compliance: access reviews, training and policy acknowledgement follow-ups, and joiner and leaver checks.

• Keep trackers and status reporting accurate, and prepare walkthroughs and answers for audit sessions.

• Automate the repetitive parts: evidence templates and exports, tracker updates, recurring evidence pulls, reminders, and checks before anything goes to an auditor.

• Bring ideas on how to structure and mature GRC as the company grows.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the role

Thndr’s Asset Management team is growing as we take on more managed mandates, and we’re looking for a Fixed Income Associate to support the team’s research and investment decisions.

In this role, you’ll spend most of your time analysing fixed income and money market instruments, following market movements, and understanding how changes in interest rates, inflation, and monetary policy affect investment opportunities.

You’ll work closely with the Head of Fixed Income, portfolio managers, and traders, providing the research and analysis they need to make informed decisions. This includes looking at Treasury Bills and Bonds, Corporate Bonds, Sukuk, and Eurobonds, as well as analysing issuers, reviewing financial statements, and keeping financial models up to date.

We’re looking for someone who enjoys working with numbers, is curious about financial markets, and can turn data and research into clear, useful insights.

What You’ll Do

  • Follow developments in fixed income and money markets, including Treasury Bills, Treasury Bonds, Corporate Bonds, Sukuk, and Eurobonds.

  • Research economic indicators, interest rates, inflation, and monetary policy, and assess how they affect the market.

  • Review companies’ financial statements to understand their financial position and assess their creditworthiness.

  • Build and update financial models to analyse yield curves, duration, convexity, and the relative value of different instruments.

  • Track daily yields, prices, auction results, and other market developments, sharing relevant updates with the team.

  • Prepare regular market updates covering yield movements, auctions, and key economic developments.

  • Support portfolio managers and traders with research ahead of auctions, new issuances, and investment decisions.

  • Monitor portfolio liquidity, upcoming maturities, and cash flow requirements across managed mandates.

  • Present your findings and investment views during team discussions and investment committee meetings.

  • Keep research files, financial models, and market databases accurate and up to date.

  • Build relationships with issuers, banks, brokers, rating agencies, and other market participants.

  • Follow internal policies and procedures, ensuring research activities comply with applicable FRA guidelines.

  • Work on ad hoc analysis and research requests from the Fixed Income team.

What You’ll Need

  • 1–4 years of experience in fixed income, money markets, or a related financial analysis role.

  • A bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or a related field.

  • A good understanding of fixed income instruments and money markets.

  • Strong financial analysis skills, including the ability to review financial statements and assess credit risk.

  • Understanding of fixed income valuation and modelling, particularly yield curves, duration, and convexity.

  • An interest in macroeconomic developments and how they affect interest rates and bond markets.

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail when working with financial data.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain findings clearly.

  • The ability to work closely with different stakeholders and manage multiple tasks.

Nice to have

  • Experience in asset management or a bank’s Treasury department, particularly ALM or a dealing room.

  • Experience in financial research or investment analysis.

  • Familiarity with the Egyptian fixed income market.

  • Experience using Bloomberg or Refinitiv Eikon.

  • Advanced Excel skills; knowledge of Python or Power BI is a plus.

  • Exposure to bond auctions, new issuances, or corporate credit analysis.

  • Experience preparing market reports or investment research.

Why this role matters

As Thndr’s managed mandates grow, the team needs solid research to understand market movements, assess risks, and make better investment decisions.

As a Fixed Income Associate, your work will help the team evaluate opportunities, understand the impact of economic changes, and make informed decisions across different fixed income instruments.

You’ll have the chance to build your expertise in fixed income markets, work closely with experienced investment professionals, and see how your analysis contributes to real investment decisions.

If you enjoy financial markets, digging into data, and understanding the reasons behind market movements, we’d love to hear from you.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

• Drive S-SDLC in our cycles and review security acceptance criteria and threat modeling.

• Guide and train the team to cover security checks and security best practices.

• Perform pre-deployment and post-deployment security penetration tests.

• Plan and execute regular web, mobile, and cloud security assessments and pen tests.

• Work closely with the Infrastructure teams to identify security issues through red teaming activities.

• Define, implement, and monitor infrastructure security measures.

• Contribute to the security roadmap & backlog.

• Assess security tools and integrate tools as needed.

• Incident Response & Research.

• Follow new security news, trends, tools, and incidents and drive needed changes.

• Support in managing our Bug-bounty program and security channels.

• Conduct vulnerability research against company assets.

• Work on understanding and improving our security logging and monitoring solutions.

• Coordinate company-wide response to security incidents till remediation.

• Vulnerability management for production/staging environments.

• Actively mentor members of the security team.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent work experience).

• Minimum 5 years of experience performing application and/or infrastructure penetration testing experience above and beyond running automated tools.

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About The Role

Alpha isn’t a chatbot sitting on top of a product. It’s an agent that reads a customer’s account, reasons about their plan, and prepares real orders for them to confirm. The model is the easy part. The hard part is everything around it: the tools it calls, the context it sees, how a request gets routed, the guardrails that keep it away from anything that must be exact, and the deterministic systems underneath that place orders, move money and consume events.

You’ll own parts of that system end to end, from spec to production. When something goes wrong in a conversation, you’ll be the one who opens the traces and finds where the run went wrong. You’ll decide whether the fix belongs in a tool, a prompt, the routing, the backend or the model, and prove it with an eval. Then you’ll explain it so product, design and other squads can act on it.

Much of the work crosses squads. Alpha integrates with Thndr’s order, funding, savings and market-data services, so you’ll write proposals other teams adopt as well as code. We also work with served models beyond Alpha, so some of the work goes below the API: choosing, evaluating, fine-tuning and serving models for other Thndr products.

We work through coding agents every day. We expect you to be very good at running your own and at helping others fix their workflows.

This is an R&D role, and we hire for breadth on purpose. Most of your time goes to Alpha, but the same person who fixes a routing failure on Monday might be benchmarking an open model, prototyping an agent for another squad, or testing whether a new technique is worth adopting by Friday. We expect you to pick up unfamiliar problems quickly, take them from research to something running in production, and know when an experiment should stop.

What You'll Do

• Own parts of Alpha end to end. Take a module, such as a tool family, the evaluation pipeline or an integration, and be accountable for how it behaves, its quality in production, and its long-term health. Don’t just follow the design we have: change it when it’s wrong.

• Design the harness. Tool contracts that read as the model’s instructions, context the model can use, routing between capabilities, and guardrails that move must-have rules out of prompt text and into code. Start from the behaviour a customer needs and work back to the component.

• Build observability and evaluation that people trust. Read traces before building dashboards. Categorise real failures and fix the most upstream one first. Build evals that check the resulting state, not just the final message. Validate LLM judges against human labels. Know the noise floor before calling something a win or a regression.

• Run Alpha like a production service. Own latency, reliability and cost for your area: time to first token, end-to-end turn latency, streaming, provider rate limits and fallbacks, and cost per conversation. Set the budgets, monitor them, and get paged when they break.

• Engineer the deterministic parts properly. Retrieval, event consumers that drive automated execution, planning and allocation logic, and integrations with money-moving services, with idempotency, retries and reconciliation. Keep the LLM away from anything that has to be exact.

• Work below the API when it pays off. Evaluate, fine-tune and serve transformer models for Alpha and other Thndr products. Run the model lifecycle like software: versioned data and evals, reproducible training, safe rollout and rollback.

• Turn questions into decisions. Take a vague “is this working?” and answer it with data: SQL over production traces, experiment design, and choosing between prompting, routing, fine-tuning or a different model. Then communicate the answer so non-specialists act on it.

• Lead cross-squad proposals. Write designs that other squads adopt for integrating Alpha with their systems, and take them from proposal to shipped.

• Raise the team’s bar. Review other engineers’ designs and evals, and help teammates improve how they work with coding agents: instructions, verification, review discipline.

• Take R&D beyond Alpha. Prototype and evaluate AI solutions for other Thndr products and squads, research new models and techniques, and turn the ones that earn it into production systems. Write up what you learned whether the experiment worked or not.

What You’ll Need

• Strong software engineering in production. You’ve built and run backend systems, ideally in Python with FastAPI, PostgreSQL and queues, and you understand how they behave under failure: slow dependencies, retries, duplicate events, deploys mid-flight.

• You’ve shipped an LLM agent or tool-calling system to real users, and you can explain the design choices: what went into the context, how tools were described, how you handled routing and failure, and what you’d change.

• You’ve owned the operations of an LLM-backed service: latency budgets including time to first token, streaming, timeouts and fallbacks, cost, and incidents.

• Measurement discipline. You’ve built evals from real traces, you know why one green run proves little, and you’ve caught a metric that looked good while the product was wrong.

• Hands-on with transformers and MLOps. You’ve fine-tuned and evaluated transformer models (SFT or LoRA) and taken a model from training to serving, with versioning and monitoring.

• Data fluency. You’re comfortable in SQL and Python analysis, and you can design an experiment and defend its conclusion.

• Ownership across the full stack. You own outcomes, not tickets: production incidents, monitoring, and the follow-up fix. You push back on the brief when it’s wrong.

• Agentic coding fluency. You work through coding agents daily, verify what they produce, and can explain how you structure that work.

• Clear written communication. Your design docs and findings get read and acted on by people outside engineering.

• Breadth and speed of learning. You’ve worked across more than one kind of problem, such as agents, retrieval, models, data or backend, and you can get productive in an unfamiliar area fast. You’re comfortable deciding what to explore and when to stop.
